+# The complete finite Henneberg characterization
+
+## Abstract
+
+Let V be any finite vertex type in any universe and G a simple graph on V. The additive Laman counts characterize an actual finite list of legal Henneberg moves starting with K2. No embedding or geometric placement is required.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (Canonical graph states).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Laman/History.State`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Laman/History.State` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Ruth Haas, David Orden, Günter Rote, Francisco Santos, Brigitte Servatius, Herman Servatius, Diane Souvaine, Ileana Streinu, Walter Whiteley (2003). *Planar Minimally Rigid Graphs and Pseudo-Triangulations*. DOI: [10.1016/j.comgeo.2004.07.003](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.comgeo.2004.07.003). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0307347v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+A state is a natural number n together with a simple graph on Fin n. There is no upper bound on n. Any graph on a finite type, in any universe, is transported to such a state by its finite enumeration isomorphism.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (The initial edge).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Laman/History.base`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Laman/History.base` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Ruth Haas, David Orden, Günter Rote, Francisco Santos, Brigitte Servatius, Herman Servatius, Diane Souvaine, Ileana Streinu, Walter Whiteley (2003). *Planar Minimally Rigid Graphs and Pseudo-Triangulations*. DOI: [10.1016/j.comgeo.2004.07.003](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.comgeo.2004.07.003). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0307347v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The base state is n=2 with the complete graph on Fin 2. The reflexive relation closure admits this graph with zero moves.
+
+**Definition 1.3 (Independently guarded legal operations).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Laman/History.Legal`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Laman/History.Legal` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Ruth Haas, David Orden, Günter Rote, Francisco Santos, Brigitte Servatius, Herman Servatius, Diane Souvaine, Ileana Streinu, Walter Whiteley (2003). *Planar Minimally Rigid Graphs and Pseudo-Triangulations*. DOI: [10.1016/j.comgeo.2004.07.003](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.comgeo.2004.07.003). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0307347v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+A legal step s to t has either two distinct old vertices a,b and an isomorphism from typeI(s.graph,a,b) to t.graph, or three old vertices a,b,c with an actual edge ab, a!=b, c!=a, c!=b and an isomorphism from typeII(s.graph,a,b,c) to t.graph. Legality does not mention Laman counts. Composing Option.some with the isomorphism gives an injective old-vertex embedding. The image of none is the unique fresh vertex, because every Option value is either none or some old vertex. Type I preserves every old adjacency and joins precisely the two selected old vertices. Type II deletes precisely the selected actual edge, preserves every other old adjacency, and joins precisely the three selected old vertices. These conclusions follow from the exhaustive Option adjacency equations of the move definitions.
+
+**Definition 1.4 (An actual finite legal list).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Laman/History.HasHistory`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Laman/History.HasHistory` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Ruth Haas, David Orden, Günter Rote, Francisco Santos, Brigitte Servatius, Herman Servatius, Diane Souvaine, Ileana Streinu, Walter Whiteley (2003). *Planar Minimally Rigid Graphs and Pseudo-Triangulations*. DOI: [10.1016/j.comgeo.2004.07.003](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.comgeo.2004.07.003). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0307347v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+HasHistory G means there is a finite list l of canonical states such that base::l is a Legal chain and G is isomorphic to its last graph. For l empty, that endpoint is base itself. No history is assumed in the counting-to-history direction.
+
+**Theorem 1.5 (Laman counts if and only if a finite legal history exists).**
+
+$$\forall V \in Type,\; [\operatorname{Finite}\left(V\right)] \forall G \in \operatorname{SimpleGraph}\left(V\right),\; ((\operatorname{edgeCount}\left(G\right) + 3 = 2 \cdot \operatorname{card}\left(V\right)) \land (\forall S \in \operatorname{Set}\left(V\right),\; (2 \le \operatorname{card}\left(S\right)) \Rightarrow (\operatorname{edgeCount}\left(\operatorname{induce}\left(G, S\right)\right) + 3 \le 2 \cdot \operatorname{card}\left(S\right)))) \Leftrightarrow (\exists l \in \operatorname{List}\left(State\right),\; (\operatorname{IsChain}\left(Legal, \operatorname{Cons}\left(base, l\right)\right)) \land (\operatorname{Nonempty}\left(\operatorname{GraphIso}\left(G, \operatorname{graph}\left(\operatorname{Last}\left(\operatorname{Cons}\left(base, l\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)))$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Laman/History.laman_iff_history` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Citation.* Ruth Haas, David Orden, Günter Rote, Francisco Santos, Brigitte Servatius, Herman Servatius, Diane Souvaine, Ileana Streinu, Walter Whiteley (2003). *Planar Minimally Rigid Graphs and Pseudo-Triangulations*. DOI: [10.1016/j.comgeo.2004.07.003](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.comgeo.2004.07.003). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0307347v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Write e(G) for the number of unordered edges, card(V) for the finite vertex count, and G[S] for the induced graph on S. The left side requires e(G)+3=2 card(V) and, for every S with card(S)>=2, e(G[S])+3<=2 card(S). The equality already forces at least two vertices, so the Lean statement also covers the empty and singleton vertex types without an extra hypothesis.
+
+Completeness uses strong induction on the actual vertex cardinality. At cardinality two, tightness identifies G with K2. Otherwise the credited safe-repair theorem supplies a degree-two deletion or a degree-three deletion with a safe actual nonedge bridge. Both smaller graphs are Laman. The induction hypothesis supplies their actual histories; reconstruction identifies G with the corresponding Option operation. Transport the smaller endpoint through its graph isomorphism, append the guarded legal step, and enumerate the new finite vertex type by Fin. The strict subtype cardinality decrease proves termination. The standard reflexive-transitive-closure/list-chain theorem then produces the required finite list.
+
+Soundness starts from the Laman K2 base and propagates the count invariant along the actual legal chain. Type I preservation and the credited Type II proof of every induced-subset inequality handle the two step cases; endpoint isomorphism transports the result back to G. The final conversion between finite subsets and arbitrary induced vertex sets preserves their exact edge counts. This is the known general Henneberg characterization; the receiving contribution is a complete finite-history construction from the credited repair and preservation proof source.
+

+# Henneberg preservation and reconstruction
+
+## Abstract
+
+Finite simple graph counts, tight subsets, and exact Henneberg operations over arbitrary vertex types.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (Laman counts).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Laman/Moves.IsLaman`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Laman/Moves.IsLaman` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Bryan Gin-ge Chen (2026). *CombinatorialRigidity, source revision 021c2284bc387efee3c3b20a18eb5f769638b578*. URL: <https://github.com/bryangingechen/CombinatorialRigidity/tree/021c2284bc387efee3c3b20a18eb5f769638b578>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every simple graph, the Laman property is (2,3)-tightness: every eligible finite subset obeys its induced-edge bound and the total edge count meets it.
+
+**Theorem 1.2 (Minimum degree in the nonbase case).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Laman/Moves.two_le_degree`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Laman/Moves.two_le_degree` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Citation.* Bryan Gin-ge Chen (2026). *CombinatorialRigidity, source revision 021c2284bc387efee3c3b20a18eb5f769638b578*. URL: <https://github.com/bryangingechen/CombinatorialRigidity/tree/021c2284bc387efee3c3b20a18eb5f769638b578>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+A Laman graph on at least three vertices has degree at least two at every vertex. Apply sparsity to the complement of that vertex and use the partition of all edges into incident and nonincident edges.
+
+**Theorem 1.3 (The two-vertex base).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Laman/Moves.eq_top_of_card_eq_two`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Laman/Moves.eq_top_of_card_eq_two` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Citation.* Bryan Gin-ge Chen (2026). *CombinatorialRigidity, source revision 021c2284bc387efee3c3b20a18eb5f769638b578*. URL: <https://github.com/bryangingechen/CombinatorialRigidity/tree/021c2284bc387efee3c3b20a18eb5f769638b578>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+A Laman graph on exactly two vertices is complete. Tightness gives one edge, and inclusion in the complete graph with the same finite edge count gives equality.
+
+**Theorem 1.4 (K2 satisfies the counts).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Laman/Moves.top_fin_two_isLaman`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Laman/Moves.top_fin_two_isLaman` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Citation.* Bryan Gin-ge Chen (2026). *CombinatorialRigidity, source revision 021c2284bc387efee3c3b20a18eb5f769638b578*. URL: <https://github.com/bryangingechen/CombinatorialRigidity/tree/021c2284bc387efee3c3b20a18eb5f769638b578>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The complete graph on Fin 2 is Laman. It has one edge, and the only eligible subset is the whole two-vertex set.
+
+**Definition 1.5 (Type I adjacency).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Laman/Moves.typeI`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Laman/Moves.typeI` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Bryan Gin-ge Chen (2026). *CombinatorialRigidity, source revision 021c2284bc387efee3c3b20a18eb5f769638b578*. URL: <https://github.com/bryangingechen/CombinatorialRigidity/tree/021c2284bc387efee3c3b20a18eb5f769638b578>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every G and old vertices a,b, the output lives on Option V. Two some-vertices are adjacent exactly when their old vertices were adjacent; none is adjacent to some u exactly when u=a or u=b; none has no loop. A legal move additionally requires a != b.
+
+**Definition 1.6 (Type II adjacency).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Laman/Moves.typeII`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Laman/Moves.typeII` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Bryan Gin-ge Chen (2026). *CombinatorialRigidity, source revision 021c2284bc387efee3c3b20a18eb5f769638b578*. URL: <https://github.com/bryangingechen/CombinatorialRigidity/tree/021c2284bc387efee3c3b20a18eb5f769638b578>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every G and old vertices a,b,c, two some-vertices remain adjacent exactly when they were adjacent and their unordered pair differs from {a,b}. The fresh none vertex is adjacent exactly to some a, some b and some c, and has no loop. A legal move requires the actual old edge ab and all three old vertices distinct.
+
+**Theorem 1.7 (Type I preserves Laman counts).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Laman/Moves.typeI_isLaman`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Laman/Moves.typeI_isLaman` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Citation.* Bryan Gin-ge Chen (2026). *CombinatorialRigidity, source revision 021c2284bc387efee3c3b20a18eb5f769638b578*. URL: <https://github.com/bryangingechen/CombinatorialRigidity/tree/021c2284bc387efee3c3b20a18eb5f769638b578>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every finite Laman G and distinct old vertices a,b, its Type I extension is Laman. For each induced subset, separate old edges from its at most two fresh edges; subsets omitting the fresh vertex inherit the old bound directly. The total count increases by two edges and one vertex.
+
+**Theorem 1.8 (Type II preserves every induced-subset bound).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Laman/Moves.typeII_isLaman`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Laman/Moves.typeII_isLaman` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Citation.* Bryan Gin-ge Chen (2026). *CombinatorialRigidity, source revision 021c2284bc387efee3c3b20a18eb5f769638b578*. URL: <https://github.com/bryangingechen/CombinatorialRigidity/tree/021c2284bc387efee3c3b20a18eb5f769638b578>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every finite Laman G, actual edge ab and third vertex c distinct from both endpoints, its Type II extension is Laman. For an induced subset, remove none to obtain its old part, subtract the bridge when present, and count the fresh incident edges. If all three neighbors occur, the deleted old edge supplies the required unit of slack. Otherwise there are at most two fresh edges; the one-vertex and empty old parts are handled separately. The proof covers every subset and does not assume planarity or placement.
+
+**Definition 1.9 (Exact Type I reconstruction).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Laman/Moves.isoTypeIOfTwoNeighbors`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Laman/Moves.isoTypeIOfTwoNeighbors` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Bryan Gin-ge Chen (2026). *CombinatorialRigidity, source revision 021c2284bc387efee3c3b20a18eb5f769638b578*. URL: <https://github.com/bryangingechen/CombinatorialRigidity/tree/021c2284bc387efee3c3b20a18eb5f769638b578>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+If the neighbors of v are exactly a and b, with both different from v, Option of the vertex-deletion subtype is isomorphic to the original graph. The equivalence sends the unique fresh none vertex to v and some w to its original old vertex; all four adjacency cases are checked.
+
+**Definition 1.10 (Exact Type II reconstruction).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Laman/Moves.isoTypeIIOfThreeNeighbors`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Laman/Moves.isoTypeIIOfThreeNeighbors` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Bryan Gin-ge Chen (2026). *CombinatorialRigidity, source revision 021c2284bc387efee3c3b20a18eb5f769638b578*. URL: <https://github.com/bryangingechen/CombinatorialRigidity/tree/021c2284bc387efee3c3b20a18eb5f769638b578>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+If the neighbors of v are exactly a,b,c, none equals v, and a,b are not adjacent in the original graph, repair the deletion graph by adding ab. Applying Type II deletes exactly that bridge. The Option/subtype equivalence preserves every other old adjacency and gives precisely the original incident edges at v.
+
+**Theorem 1.11 (A smaller Laman graph).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Laman/Moves.exists_typeI_or_typeII_reverse`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Laman/Moves.exists_typeI_or_typeII_reverse` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Citation.* Bryan Gin-ge Chen (2026). *CombinatorialRigidity, source revision 021c2284bc387efee3c3b20a18eb5f769638b578*. URL: <https://github.com/bryangingechen/CombinatorialRigidity/tree/021c2284bc387efee3c3b20a18eb5f769638b578>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Every finite Laman graph on at least three vertices admits a Type I or Type II reverse to a Laman graph on the subtype excluding one vertex. Minimum degree excludes the pendant case. Type I tightness follows by reconstruction and reverse preservation; Type II tightness follows from the safe sparse repair, the actual bridge edge, and the exact edge count.

+# Safe nonedge repair by tight blockers
+
+## Abstract
+

+# Sparsity and tight-set closure
+
+## Abstract
+

+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every vertex type V, graph G and set S of vertices, edgesIn G S consists of the actual edges of G whose two endpoints lie in S. The map induced by subtype inclusion identifies it bijectively with the edge set of G induced on S.

+**Definition 1.2 (Additive sparsity).**

+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Laman/SparseSets.IsSparse`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Laman/SparseSets.IsSparse` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Bryan Gin-ge Chen (2026). *CombinatorialRigidity, source revision 021c2284bc387efee3c3b20a18eb5f769638b578*. URL: <https://github.com/bryangingechen/CombinatorialRigidity/tree/021c2284bc387efee3c3b20a18eb5f769638b578>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every graph G and natural numbers k and ell, sparsity requires e(s)+ell <= k card(s) for every finite vertex set s for which ell <= k card(s). The additive convention avoids truncated natural subtraction.

+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Laman/SparseSets.IsTight` (`✓ std3`).

+theorem IsSparse.contradiction_three_pair
+    [Finite V] {G : SimpleGraph V} (h : G.IsSparse 2 3) {v a b c : V}
+    (ha : G.Adj v a) (hb : G.Adj v b) (hc : G.Adj v c)
+    (hab : a ≠ b) (hac : a ≠ c) (hbc : b ≠ c)
+    (hbc_nadj : ¬ G.Adj b c)
+    {Sab : Finset V} (hvSab : v ∉ Sab) (haSab : a ∈ Sab) (hbSab : b ∈ Sab)
+    (hSab_tight : G.IsTightOn 2 3 Sab)
+    {Sac : Finset V} (hvSac : v ∉ Sac) (haSac : a ∈ Sac) (hcSac : c ∈ Sac)
+    (hSac_tight : G.IsTightOn 2 3 Sac)
+    {Sbc : Finset V} (hvSbc : v ∉ Sbc) (hbSbc : b ∈ Sbc) (hcSbc : c ∈ Sbc)
+    (hSbc_tight : G.IsTightOn 2 3 Sbc) : False := by
+  classical
+  by_cases h_ab_ac : 2 ≤ (Sab ∩ Sac).card
+  · exact IsSparse.contradiction_pair_aux h ha hb hc hab hac hbc hvSab hvSac
+      (Finset.mem_union_left _ haSab) (Finset.mem_union_left _ hbSab)
+      (Finset.mem_union_right _ hcSac) hSab_tight hSac_tight h_ab_ac
+  by_cases h_ab_bc : 2 ≤ (Sab ∩ Sbc).card
+  · exact IsSparse.contradiction_pair_aux h ha hb hc hab hac hbc hvSab hvSbc
+      (Finset.mem_union_left _ haSab) (Finset.mem_union_left _ hbSab)
+      (Finset.mem_union_right _ hcSbc) hSab_tight hSbc_tight h_ab_bc
+  by_cases h_ac_bc : 2 ≤ (Sac ∩ Sbc).card
+  · exact IsSparse.contradiction_pair_aux h ha hb hc hab hac hbc hvSac hvSbc
+      (Finset.mem_union_left _ haSac) (Finset.mem_union_right _ hbSbc)
+      (Finset.mem_union_left _ hcSac) hSac_tight hSbc_tight h_ac_bc
+  push Not at h_ab_ac h_ab_bc h_ac_bc
+  have hab_ac_card : (Sab ∩ Sac).card = 1 := by
+    have : 1 ≤ (Sab ∩ Sac).card :=
+      Finset.card_pos.mpr ⟨a, Finset.mem_inter.mpr ⟨haSab, haSac⟩⟩
+    omega
+  have hab_bc_card : (Sab ∩ Sbc).card = 1 := by
+    have : 1 ≤ (Sab ∩ Sbc).card :=
+      Finset.card_pos.mpr ⟨b, Finset.mem_inter.mpr ⟨hbSab, hbSbc⟩⟩
+    omega
+  have hac_bc_card : (Sac ∩ Sbc).card = 1 := by
+    have : 1 ≤ (Sac ∩ Sbc).card :=
+      Finset.card_pos.mpr ⟨c, Finset.mem_inter.mpr ⟨hcSac, hcSbc⟩⟩
+    omega
+  have hab_ac_eq : Sab ∩ Sac = {a} :=
+    Finset.eq_singleton_of_mem_of_card_le_one
+      (Finset.mem_inter.mpr ⟨haSab, haSac⟩) (by omega)
+  have hab_bc_eq : Sab ∩ Sbc = {b} :=
+    Finset.eq_singleton_of_mem_of_card_le_one
+      (Finset.mem_inter.mpr ⟨hbSab, hbSbc⟩) (by omega)
+  have hac_bc_eq : Sac ∩ Sbc = {c} :=
+    Finset.eq_singleton_of_mem_of_card_le_one
+      (Finset.mem_inter.mpr ⟨hcSac, hcSbc⟩) (by omega)
+  have h_e_inter_ab_ac : (G.edgesIn (↑(Sab ∩ Sac) : Set V)).ncard = 0 := by
+    rw [hab_ac_eq, Finset.coe_singleton, edgesIn_singleton]
+    exact Set.ncard_empty _
+  have h_super_12 : (G.edgesIn (↑Sab : Set V)).ncard + (G.edgesIn (↑Sac : Set V)).ncard
+      ≤ (G.edgesIn (↑(Sab ∪ Sac) : Set V)).ncard := by
+    have h_super := G.edgesIn_ncard_add_le (↑Sab : Set V) (↑Sac : Set V)
+    have h_eq_union : (↑(Sab ∪ Sac) : Set V) = ↑Sab ∪ ↑Sac := Finset.coe_union _ _
+    have h_eq_inter : (G.edgesIn (↑Sab ∩ ↑Sac : Set V)).ncard = 0 := by
+      rw [← Finset.coe_inter]; exact h_e_inter_ab_ac
+    rw [h_eq_union]
+    omega
+  have hT12_card : (Sab ∪ Sac).card = Sab.card + Sac.card - 1 := by
+    have h1 := Finset.card_union_add_card_inter Sab Sac
+    rw [hab_ac_card] at h1
+    omega
+  have h_T12_inter_Sbc_eq : (Sab ∪ Sac) ∩ Sbc = ({b, c} : Finset V) := by
+    rw [Finset.union_inter_distrib_right, hab_bc_eq, hac_bc_eq]
+    rfl
+  have h_T12_inter_Sbc_card : ((Sab ∪ Sac) ∩ Sbc).card = 2 := by
+    rw [h_T12_inter_Sbc_eq, Finset.card_pair hbc]
+  have h_e_inter_T12_Sbc : (G.edgesIn (↑((Sab ∪ Sac) ∩ Sbc) : Set V)).ncard = 0 := by
+    suffices h : G.edgesIn (↑((Sab ∪ Sac) ∩ Sbc) : Set V) = ∅ by
+      rw [h]; exact Set.ncard_empty _
+    rw [h_T12_inter_Sbc_eq]
+    ext e
+    refine e.ind fun p q => ?_
+    simp only [Finset.coe_insert, Finset.coe_singleton, mem_edgesIn, mem_edgeSet, Sym2.coe_mk,
+               Set.insert_subset_iff, Set.singleton_subset_iff, Set.mem_insert_iff,
+               Set.mem_singleton_iff, Set.mem_empty_iff_false, iff_false, not_and]
+    intro h_adj h_p h_q
+    rcases h_p with rfl | rfl <;> rcases h_q with rfl | rfl
+    · exact G.loopless.irrefl _ h_adj
+    · exact hbc_nadj h_adj
+    · exact hbc_nadj h_adj.symm
+    · exact G.loopless.irrefl _ h_adj
+  set T : Finset V := (Sab ∪ Sac) ∪ Sbc with hT_def
+  have h_super_T : (G.edgesIn (↑(Sab ∪ Sac) : Set V)).ncard +
+      (G.edgesIn (↑Sbc : Set V)).ncard ≤ (G.edgesIn (↑T : Set V)).ncard := by
+    have h_super := G.edgesIn_ncard_add_le (↑(Sab ∪ Sac) : Set V) (↑Sbc : Set V)
+    have h_eq_union : (↑T : Set V) = ↑(Sab ∪ Sac) ∪ ↑Sbc := by
+      rw [hT_def]; exact Finset.coe_union _ _
+    have h_eq_inter : (G.edgesIn (↑(Sab ∪ Sac) ∩ ↑Sbc : Set V)).ncard = 0 := by
+      rw [← Finset.coe_inter]; exact h_e_inter_T12_Sbc
+    rw [h_eq_union]
+    omega
+  have hT_card : T.card = Sab.card + Sac.card + Sbc.card - 3 := by
+    have h1 := Finset.card_union_add_card_inter (Sab ∪ Sac) Sbc
+    rw [h_T12_inter_Sbc_card, hT12_card, ← hT_def] at h1
+    have hT12_ge : 1 ≤ (Sab ∪ Sac).card :=
+      Finset.card_pos.mpr ⟨a, Finset.mem_union_left _ haSab⟩
+    omega
+  have hvT : v ∉ T := by
+    simp only [hT_def, Finset.mem_union, not_or]
+    exact ⟨⟨hvSab, hvSac⟩, hvSbc⟩
+  have haT : a ∈ T := Finset.mem_union_left _ (Finset.mem_union_left _ haSab)
+  have hbT : b ∈ T := Finset.mem_union_left _ (Finset.mem_union_left _ hbSab)
+  have hcT : c ∈ T := Finset.mem_union_left _ (Finset.mem_union_right _ hcSac)
+  have hT_card_ge : 3 ≤ T.card :=
+    Finset.two_lt_card_iff.mpr ⟨a, b, c, haT, hbT, hcT, hab, hac, hbc⟩
+  have hT_tight : G.IsTightOn 2 3 T := h.isTightOn_of_le (by omega) (by
+    grind only [IsTightOn])
+  exact IsSparse.no_isTightOn_excluding_three_neighbors h ha hb hc hab hac hbc
+    hvT haT hbT hcT hT_tight
+

+theorem IsSparse.typeII_reverse_blocker
+    [Finite V] {G : SimpleGraph V} (h : G.IsSparse 2 3) {v x y : V}
+    (hxv : x ≠ v) (hyv : y ≠ v)
+    (h_not_sparse : ¬ (G.comap (Subtype.val : {w : V // w ≠ v} → V) ⊔
+                       fromEdgeSet ({s(⟨x, hxv⟩, ⟨y, hyv⟩)} : Set (Sym2 _))).IsSparse 2 3) :
+    ∃ S : Finset V, v ∉ S ∧ x ∈ S ∧ y ∈ S ∧ G.IsTightOn 2 3 S := by
+  classical
+  set f : {w : V // w ≠ v} → V := Subtype.val with hf_def
+  set xs : {w : V // w ≠ v} := ⟨x, hxv⟩ with hxs_def
+  set ys : {w : V // w ≠ v} := ⟨y, hyv⟩ with hys_def
+  set bridge : Sym2 {w : V // w ≠ v} := s(xs, ys) with hbridge_def
+  set G' : SimpleGraph {w : V // w ≠ v} :=
+    G.comap f ⊔ fromEdgeSet ({bridge} : Set _) with hG'_def
+  unfold IsSparse at h_not_sparse
+  push Not at h_not_sparse
+  obtain ⟨s', hs'_card, hviol⟩ := h_not_sparse
+  set S : Finset V := s'.image f with hS_def
+  have hS_card : S.card = s'.card :=
+    Finset.card_image_of_injective s' Subtype.val_injective
+  have hvS : v ∉ S := by
+    intro hmem
+    obtain ⟨w, _, hw⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hmem
+    exact w.2 hw
+  have h_link : ((G.comap f).edgesIn (↑s' : Set _)).ncard = (G.edgesIn (↑S : Set V)).ncard :=
+    G.ncard_edgesIn_comap Subtype.val_injective s'
+  have hS_sparse : (G.edgesIn (↑S : Set V)).ncard + 3 ≤ 2 * S.card := by
+    have := h S (by rw [hS_card]; exact hs'_card)
+    exact this
+  by_cases h_both : xs ∈ s' ∧ ys ∈ s'
+  · obtain ⟨hxs_in, hys_in⟩ := h_both
+    have h_subset : G'.edgesIn (↑s' : Set _) ⊆
+        (G.comap f).edgesIn (↑s' : Set _) ∪ ({bridge} : Set _) := by
+      intro e he
+      rw [mem_edgesIn] at he
+      obtain ⟨he_edge, he_sub⟩ := he
+      rw [hG'_def, edgeSet_sup] at he_edge
+      rcases he_edge with hin_comap | hin_bridge
+      · exact Or.inl (mem_edgesIn.mpr ⟨hin_comap, he_sub⟩)
+      · rw [edgeSet_fromEdgeSet] at hin_bridge
+        exact Or.inr (Set.sdiff_subset hin_bridge)
+    have h_ncard_bound : (G'.edgesIn (↑s' : Set _)).ncard ≤
+        (G.edgesIn (↑S : Set V)).ncard + 1 :=
+      calc (G'.edgesIn (↑s' : Set _)).ncard
+          ≤ ((G.comap f).edgesIn (↑s' : Set _) ∪ ({bridge} : Set _)).ncard :=
+            Set.ncard_le_ncard h_subset (Set.toFinite _)
+        _ ≤ ((G.comap f).edgesIn (↑s' : Set _)).ncard + ({bridge} : Set _).ncard :=
+            Set.ncard_union_le _ _
+        _ = (G.edgesIn (↑S : Set V)).ncard + 1 := by
+            rw [h_link, Set.ncard_singleton]
+    have hx_in_S : x ∈ S := by
+      simp only [hS_def, Finset.mem_image]
+      exact ⟨xs, hxs_in, rfl⟩
+    have hy_in_S : y ∈ S := by
+      simp only [hS_def, Finset.mem_image]
+      exact ⟨ys, hys_in, rfl⟩
+    refine ⟨S, hvS, hx_in_S, hy_in_S, ?_⟩
+    refine h.isTightOn_of_le ?_ ?_
+    · rw [hS_card]; exact hs'_card
+    · rw [hS_card]; omega
+  · have h_subset : G'.edgesIn (↑s' : Set _) ⊆ (G.comap f).edgesIn (↑s' : Set _) := by
+      intro e he
+      rw [mem_edgesIn] at he ⊢
+      obtain ⟨he_edge, he_sub⟩ := he
+      refine ⟨?_, he_sub⟩
+      rw [hG'_def, edgeSet_sup] at he_edge
+      rcases he_edge with hin_comap | hin_bridge
+      · exact hin_comap
+      · rw [edgeSet_fromEdgeSet, Set.mem_sdiff, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hin_bridge
+        obtain ⟨rfl, _⟩ := hin_bridge
+        rw [hbridge_def, Sym2.coe_mk, Set.insert_subset_iff,
+            Set.singleton_subset_iff, Finset.mem_coe, Finset.mem_coe] at he_sub
+        exact absurd he_sub h_both
+    have h_ncard_bound : (G'.edgesIn (↑s' : Set _)).ncard ≤
+        (G.edgesIn (↑S : Set V)).ncard := by
+      rw [← h_link]
+      exact Set.ncard_le_ncard h_subset (Set.toFinite _)
+    exfalso
+    rw [hS_card] at hS_sparse
+    omega

+    {v : V} (x y c : {w : V // w ≠ v})

+lemma image_edgesIn_comap (G : SimpleGraph V) {V' : Type*} (f : V' → V) (s' : Set V') :
+    Sym2.map f '' ((G.comap f).edgesIn s') = G.edgesIn (f '' s') := by
+  ext e
+  refine e.ind fun p q => ?_
+  rw [Sym2.mk_mem_image_map_iff]
+  simp only [mem_edgesIn, mem_edgeSet, comap_adj, Sym2.coe_mk, Set.insert_subset_iff,
+             Set.singleton_subset_iff, Set.mem_image]
+  constructor
+  · rintro ⟨u, w, rfl, rfl, hadj, hu, hw⟩
+    exact ⟨hadj, ⟨u, hu, rfl⟩, ⟨w, hw, rfl⟩⟩
+  · rintro ⟨hadj, ⟨u, hu, rfl⟩, ⟨w, hw, rfl⟩⟩
+    exact ⟨u, w, rfl, rfl, hadj, hu, hw⟩

+lemma ncard_edgesIn_comap [DecidableEq V] {V' : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V)
+    {f : V' → V} (hf : Function.Injective f) (s' : Finset V') :

+theorem IsSparse.iso {W : Type*} {G : SimpleGraph V} {H : SimpleGraph W}
+    (φ : G ≃g H) {k ℓ : ℕ} (h : G.IsSparse k ℓ) : H.IsSparse k ℓ := by
+  classical
+  intro s hs
+  set s' : Finset V := s.image φ.symm
+  have hs'_card : s'.card = s.card :=
+    Finset.card_image_of_injective s φ.symm.toEquiv.injective
+  have h_eq : (H.edgesIn (↑s : Set W)).ncard = (G.edgesIn (↑s' : Set V)).ncard := by
+    rw [show (↑s' : Set V) = φ.symm '' ↑s from Finset.coe_image, ← Iso.image_edgesIn φ.symm,
+      Set.ncard_image_of_injective _ (Sym2.map.injective φ.symm.injective)]
+  rw [h_eq, ← hs'_card]
+  exact h s' (hs'_card ▸ hs)
+
+theorem IsTight.iso {W : Type*} {G : SimpleGraph V} {H : SimpleGraph W}
+    (φ : G ≃g H) {k ℓ : ℕ} (h : G.IsTight k ℓ) : H.IsTight k ℓ := by
+  refine ⟨h.1.iso φ, ?_⟩
+  have hE : H.edgeSet.ncard = G.edgeSet.ncard := by
+    simp only [← Nat.card_coe_set_eq]
+    exact Nat.card_congr φ.mapEdgeSet.symm
+  have hV : Nat.card W = Nat.card V := Nat.card_congr φ.toEquiv.symm
+  grind only [h.2]
+
+theorem IsSparse.comap {V' : Type*} {G : SimpleGraph V} {k ℓ : ℕ} (h : G.IsSparse k ℓ)
+    {f : V' → V} (hf : Function.Injective f) : (G.comap f).IsSparse k ℓ := by
+  classical
+  intro s' hs'
+  set S : Finset V := s'.image f
+  have hS_card : S.card = s'.card := Finset.card_image_of_injective s' hf
+  have h_link : ((G.comap f).edgesIn (↑s' : Set V')).ncard = (G.edgesIn (↑S : Set V)).ncard :=
+    G.ncard_edgesIn_comap hf s'
+  rw [h_link, ← hS_card]
+  exact h S (hS_card ▸ hs')

+theorem IsSparse.isTightOn_of_le {G : SimpleGraph V} {k ℓ : ℕ}
+    (hG : G.IsSparse k ℓ) {s : Finset V} (hs : ℓ ≤ k * s.card)
+    (h_le : k * s.card ≤ (G.edgesIn ↑s).ncard + ℓ) :

+theorem IsTightOn.union_inter [Finite V] [DecidableEq V] {G : SimpleGraph V} {k ℓ : ℕ}
+    {s t : Finset V} (hs : G.IsTightOn k ℓ s) (ht : G.IsTightOn k ℓ t)
+    (hG : G.IsSparse k ℓ) (h_inter : ℓ ≤ k * (s ∩ t).card) :
+    G.IsTightOn k ℓ (s ∪ t) ∧ G.IsTightOn k ℓ (s ∩ t) := by
+  have h_super := G.edgesIn_ncard_add_le (↑s : Set V) (↑t : Set V)
+  rw [← Finset.coe_union, ← Finset.coe_inter] at h_super
+  have h_sparse_inter := hG (s ∩ t) h_inter
+  have h_sparse_union := hG (s ∪ t)
+    (h_inter.trans (Nat.mul_le_mul_left k (Finset.card_le_card Finset.inter_subset_union)))
+  have h_card_mul := Finset.mul_card_union_add_mul_card_inter s t k
+  grind only [IsTightOn]

+theorem IsTightOn.union_with_bonus [Finite V] [DecidableEq V] {G : SimpleGraph V} {k ℓ : ℕ}
+    {S₁ S₂ : Finset V} (h₁ : G.IsTightOn k ℓ S₁) (h₂ : G.IsTightOn k ℓ S₂)
+    (hG : G.IsSparse k ℓ) {F : Set (Sym2 V)}
+    (hF_sub : F ⊆ G.edgesIn (↑(S₁ ∪ S₂) : Set V))
+    (hF_disj : Disjoint F (G.edgesIn (↑S₁ : Set V) ∪ G.edgesIn (↑S₂ : Set V)))
+    (h_close : (G.edgesIn (↑(S₁ ∩ S₂) : Set V)).ncard + ℓ ≤
+               F.ncard + k * (S₁ ∩ S₂).card) :
+    G.IsTightOn k ℓ (S₁ ∪ S₂) := by
+  have h_un_sub :
+      G.edgesIn (↑S₁ : Set V) ∪ G.edgesIn (↑S₂ : Set V) ⊆ G.edgesIn (↑(S₁ ∪ S₂) : Set V) := by
+    rw [Finset.coe_union]
+    exact Set.union_subset (edgesIn_mono Set.subset_union_left)
+                           (edgesIn_mono Set.subset_union_right)
+  have h_combined_sub :
+      G.edgesIn (↑S₁ : Set V) ∪ G.edgesIn (↑S₂ : Set V) ∪ F ⊆ G.edgesIn (↑(S₁ ∪ S₂) : Set V) :=
+    Set.union_subset h_un_sub hF_sub
+  have h_inter_eq : G.edgesIn (↑S₁ : Set V) ∩ G.edgesIn (↑S₂ : Set V) =
+                    G.edgesIn (↑(S₁ ∩ S₂) : Set V) := by
+    rw [Finset.coe_inter]; exact (edgesIn_inter _ _).symm
+  have h_un_card :
+      (G.edgesIn (↑S₁ : Set V) ∪ G.edgesIn (↑S₂ : Set V)).ncard +
+        (G.edgesIn (↑(S₁ ∩ S₂) : Set V)).ncard =
+        (G.edgesIn (↑S₁ : Set V)).ncard + (G.edgesIn (↑S₂ : Set V)).ncard := by
+    rw [← h_inter_eq]; exact Set.ncard_union_add_ncard_inter _ _
+  have h_combined_card :
+      (G.edgesIn (↑S₁ : Set V) ∪ G.edgesIn (↑S₂ : Set V) ∪ F).ncard =
+        (G.edgesIn (↑S₁ : Set V) ∪ G.edgesIn (↑S₂ : Set V)).ncard + F.ncard :=
+    Set.ncard_union_eq hF_disj.symm
+      ((G.edgesIn_finite S₁).union (G.edgesIn_finite S₂)) ((G.edgesIn_finite _).subset hF_sub)
+  have h_le_union :=
+    Set.ncard_le_ncard h_combined_sub (G.edgesIn_finite (S₁ ∪ S₂))
+  have h_card_mul := Finset.mul_card_union_add_mul_card_inter S₁ S₂ k
+  have h_S1_size : ℓ ≤ k * S₁.card := by grind only [IsTightOn]
+  have h_union_size : ℓ ≤ k * (S₁ ∪ S₂).card :=
+    h_S1_size.trans (Nat.mul_le_mul_left k (Finset.card_le_card Finset.subset_union_left))
+  refine hG.isTightOn_of_le h_union_size ?_
+  grind only [IsTightOn]
+
+theorem IsTightOn.insert_vertex_with_edges [DecidableEq V] {G : SimpleGraph V}
+    {k ℓ : ℕ} {S : Finset V} (h : G.IsTightOn k ℓ S) (hG : G.IsSparse k ℓ)
+    {w : V} (hw : w ∉ S) {F : Set (Sym2 V)}
+    (hF_sub : F ⊆ G.edgesIn (↑(insert w S) : Set V))
+    (hF_disj : Disjoint F (G.edgesIn (↑S : Set V))) (h_card : k ≤ F.ncard) :
+    G.IsTightOn k ℓ (insert w S) := by
+  have h_S_sub : G.edgesIn (↑S : Set V) ⊆ G.edgesIn (↑(insert w S) : Set V) := by
+    refine edgesIn_mono ?_; rw [Finset.coe_insert]; exact Set.subset_insert _ _
+  have h_combined_sub :
+      G.edgesIn (↑S : Set V) ∪ F ⊆ G.edgesIn (↑(insert w S) : Set V) :=
+    Set.union_subset h_S_sub hF_sub
+  have h_combined_card :
+      (G.edgesIn (↑S : Set V) ∪ F).ncard = (G.edgesIn (↑S : Set V)).ncard + F.ncard :=
+    Set.ncard_union_eq hF_disj.symm (G.edgesIn_finite S) ((G.edgesIn_finite _).subset hF_sub)
+  have h_le := Set.ncard_le_ncard h_combined_sub (G.edgesIn_finite (insert w S))
+  have h_card_insert : (insert w S).card = S.card + 1 := Finset.card_insert_of_notMem hw
+  have h_size : ℓ ≤ k * (insert w S).card := by
+    unfold IsTightOn at h
+    rw [h_card_insert, Nat.mul_add, Nat.mul_one]; omega
+  refine hG.isTightOn_of_le h_size ?_
+  rw [h_card_insert, Nat.mul_add, Nat.mul_one] at h_size ⊢
+  grind only [IsTightOn]
+
+end SimpleGraph

+
+# Henneberg characterization of Laman graphs
+
+Section 2, pages 4–5, starts the construction with an edge on two vertices. Type I joins a fresh vertex to two old vertices. Type II removes an edge and joins a fresh vertex to its two endpoints and a third vertex. The text explicitly says these constructions work for general, not necessarily planar, Laman graphs. Lemma 2.1 states that a graph is Laman if and only if it has a Henneberg construction. Its reverse proof removes a suitable degree-two or degree-three vertex while preserving the Laman property.
+
+This is a known general combinatorial theorem. No planar embedding or generic geometric placement is a hypothesis of the receiving finite-history theorem. Laman's original DOI is 10.1007/BF01534980; its full original text is not used as a verified locator here.
